name: realm-web SDK import
what: realm-web is the Atlas Device SDK for the browser; its App Services login and sync path reached end-of-life

name: Realm.App client init
what: Realm.App({ id }) points the client at an Atlas App Services app ID that no longer serves Device Sync
fix: new PowerSyncDatabase({ schema, database: { dbFilename } }) then db.connect(connector)

name: Flexible Sync configuration
what: Flexible Sync config opens a Device Sync session
fix: move the query into PowerSync Sync Rules (bucket_definitions: parameters + data queries)

name: Flexible Sync subscriptions
what: client-side sync subscriptions are a Device Sync feature
fix: declare what each user receives server-side in PowerSync Sync Rules; read locally with db.getAll('SELECT ...')

name: Partition-based sync
what: partitionValue is legacy partition-based Device Sync
fix: turn the partition key into a PowerSync bucket parameter (e.g. request.user_id())

name: Atlas Data API base URL
what: the Atlas Data API endpoint reached end-of-life
fix: call your own backend (MongoDB driver) instead, or read the synced local copy through PowerSync

name: Custom HTTPS Endpoint URL
what: App Services custom HTTPS Endpoints reached end-of-life
fix: host the route on your own API; PowerSync writes go through connector.uploadData()

name: Data API key header
what: an api-key header for the Data API (a server secret in client code)
fix: drop it; PowerSync clients authenticate with a short-lived JWT from connector.fetchCredentials()

name: Data API action call
fix: reads: db.getAll / db.watch on the local SQLite copy; writes: db.execute, uploaded by connector.uploadData()

name: App Services login credentials
what: App Services authentication through the Device SDK
fix: keep your own auth (Auth0, Supabase, Firebase, custom JWT) and return its token from fetchCredentials()

name: Remote mongoClient
what: user.mongoClient() queries Atlas through App Services from the device
fix: query the local database with db.getAll('SELECT ...'); server-side changes arrive through Sync Rules

name: Function call through the SDK
what: calling an App Services function through the Device SDK client
fix: expose the logic as an endpoint on your own backend and call it from the app or from uploadData()

name: @realm/react sync providers
what: @realm/react AppProvider/UserProvider wire the app to App Services

name: Sync session control
fix: db.connect(connector) / db.disconnect(); wait with db.waitForFirstSync(); status in db.currentStatus

name: Native Realm sync SDK
what: a Swift, Kotlin or Dart Realm SDK used with Device Sync
fix: PowerSync Swift SDK, Kotlin Multiplatform SDK (com.powersync) or package:powersync/powersync.dart

name: App Services client API URL
what: the App Services client API that Device SDK login and GraphQL traffic used
fix: point the app at your own auth and API; the PowerSync endpoint comes from fetchCredentials()
